entry.title: Xbox to Publish Kojima Productions' Physint After PlayStation Exit
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The espionage game Physint will be published by Xbox after PlayStation Studios rescinded its partnership with Kojima Productions. This new agreement also includes expanded collaboration across film and television to reach broader audiences.

Hideo Kojima sought a new partner for three months after receiving notice from PlayStation to cancel the project. Through this expanded partnership, Xbox will also support the studio's upcoming project, OD - Knock.

entry.title: Turnkey Games Founders Discuss Transitioning from AAA to Indie Development
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Former id Software employees Tony Garza and Richard O'Neal founded Turnkey Games to gain creative control and bypass the instability of AAA studio environments. They advocate for a lean, bootstrapped development model that prioritizes core gameplay features and avoids the excessive technical scaling and scope creep typical of large-scale studio productions.

The studio's methodology for the development of their debut title, Apart, emphasizes maintaining momentum through iterative design and "good enough" solutions to manage budgets. While the founders highlight the rewards of direct ownership, they note that indie development requires managing significantly more personal financial, technical, and operational risk.

entry.title: No Man's Sky Releases Cosmos Update 7.0
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | nomanssky.com | hacker news

The Cosmos update (version 7.0) for No Man's Sky adds space station directorship, orbital construction, and deep-space outposts. Players can customize station interiors, build habitats in space, and salvage resources from derelict shipwrecks. New features also include an interactive star system map and the ability to fly directly to stars.

To celebrate the game's 10th anniversary, the update includes the "Our Journey Continues" expedition, which offers rewards like the Starbound v0.27 Multi-Tool and a vintage Sentinel Interceptor. Visual improvements include enhanced terrain tessellation and updated particle lighting, while new mechanics introduce galactic alliances and star system navigation.

entry.title: Mark Cerny and Geoff Keighley Launch Nova Games Foundation Fellowship Program
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The Nova Games Foundation provides grants to emerging game designers through a university-affiliated fellowship program. Established by Mark Cerny and Geoff Keighley, the initiative awards $100,000 to 20 young developers annually, with select fellows eligible for up to $500,000 based on milestone achievement. These "no-strings-attached" funds allow recipients to retain full ownership of their projects without providing equity to the foundation.

In addition to funding, the foundation offers mentorship from industry leaders, including Josef Fares. This initiative follows the indefinite suspension of Keighley's previous "Future Class" program, which faced criticism for a perceived lack of practical support for emerging professionals. The first cohort of Nova fellows is scheduled for announcement in March 2027.

entry.title: Valve Discusses Steam Platform Growth and Developer Support
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com

At GDC, Valve representatives Tom Jardino and Casey presented data regarding Steam's user growth and developer success. The platform has reached 42 million peak concurrent users and 13.9 million in-game users, effectively doubling its scale over the last five years. During this period, the number of games achieving over $100,000 in annual revenue has nearly doubled, rising from 3,000 in 2020 to 5,800 in 2025.

Valve emphasized that its private, non-advertiser-funded structure allows the company to prioritize long-term platform stability and user satisfaction over short-term quarterly earnings. The presentation highlighted several development initiatives, including the use of Steam Labs to iteratively test new features and efforts to address localized user review trends to prevent regional issues from unfairly impacting a game's global rating.

entry.title: Riot Games Considering Expansion into Premium Games
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Co-founder Marc Merrill has indicated that the studio is evaluating premium, single-purchase models to complement its free-to-play portfolio. Speaking at PAX West 2026, Merrill noted that while free-to-play is effective for long-term engagement through cosmetic sales, premium models may be better suited for certain genres to preserve design integrity.

This potential shift follows the decision to wind down development on the fighting game 2XKO. Merrill also reiterated the studio's ambition to develop a massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG), a project he described as "the Grail."

entry.title: White House Removes Tetris Clone Following The Tetris Company Copyright Warning
entry.content:
Techmeme | kotaku.com | source

The White House has removed "Build the Wall," a game modeled after Tetris, from its web arcade portal. The removal follows a public statement from The Tetris Company, which distanced itself from the project and warned that it takes copyright infringement very seriously.

The game was part of a series of controversial web titles launched by the administration that used popular video game motifs to convey political themes. This incident represents a significant instance of a major gaming company signaling potential legal action against the government regarding the unauthorized use of intellectual property.

entry.title: EA Sports Reportedly Using Generative AI for NHL 27 Voiceover
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Sports commentator John Buccigross claims that EA Sports is utilizing generative AI to create voiceover for in-game commentary in the upcoming professional hockey simulator NHL 27. During an appearance on the Chirpin Zebras podcast, Buccigross stated that while the technology is impressive, it still requires human intervention to correct semantic errors, such as using "chairs" instead of "seats."

This development aligns with a long-term strategy by EA CEO Andrew Wilson to integrate generative AI into core development processes. The company has previously partnered with Stability AI to co-develop tools and workflows aimed at reimagining content creation.

entry.title: Tim Schafer Discusses Double Fine's Business Strategy and Independence from Xbox
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The head of Double Fine Productions, Tim Schafer, has dismissed claims that the studio's games are merely niche "arthouse" projects, asserting they possess mass market potential. Following the studio's separation from Xbox during a corporate restructuring in July, the studio has returned to independent status, a transition that included the layoff of 23 staff members to ensure long-term sustainability.

To diversify revenue, the studio is pursuing game ports, remasters, and new investment while developing a new publishing label, Double Fine Action Labs. This label will release small games produced via the Amnesia Fortnight game jam, which is currently supported by a Kickstarter campaign that has significantly exceeded its $400,000 goal.

entry.title: FuturLab Lays Off Seven Employees After Cancelling Unannounced Project
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Seven employees have been laid off at FuturLab following the cancellation of a project that had been in development for two to three years. Studio CEO Kirsty Rigden stated the project, which was unrelated to PowerWash Simulator, was scrapped during pre-production because projected development costs were expected to exceed potential revenue.

Sources familiar with the situation allege that staff were left without assigned work for several weeks in June 2026 after the project was shelved. Managers and team leads were reportedly not informed of the upcoming layoffs, and employees were allegedly instructed to use the term "the leavers" rather than "redundancy" when describing the departures.
